title: Prototypes live in DISCOVERY as evidence; code is burned; salvage is re-derivation
context: DEFINE step 3 (spec 2026-10-01, section 5) asks where a learning prototype belongs. A prototype is useful for the questions it provokes; its code is a product of exploration under a different set of rules than the project proper, so promoting it would smuggle unowned decisions past the chain.
decision: prototypes live in DISCOVERY as evidence; code is burned; salvage is re-derivation. The prototype is recorded in the intake classification as an artefact of kind `other`; its outputs are brief statements with source spans `prototype:<name>:<observation>`; the burn is a single `constraint` statement naming the prototype, its commit sha and burn date. The only middle path is salvage by re-derivation: extract requirements from the prototype as evidence, run them through intake and the PO loop like any document, rebuild from the tree.
consequences: Provenance stays whole: every shape in the tree has a chain back to a PO-sanctioned statement, not a prototype's incidental choices. The cost is one managed-block rule the harness picks up, one guidance file (`guidance/discovery-prototypes.md`) and the honest message that a prototype's code is reference only; nothing in the build consumes a prototype directly.

alternativesConsidered.name: A prototype mode or promotion path (inverts provenance)
alternativesConsidered.summary: Keep the prototype as a privileged tree that can be promoted into the project tree, or run a prototype mode that bypasses parts of the chain while the prototype is live.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Promotion inverts provenance: a shape would reach the project tree without the PO loop that owns every settled shape. The method's whole worth is that every requirement, story, AC and shape has a known origin; a promotion path would let an incidental prototype choice bypass that trace, and no amount of auditing after the fact can restore the owner.
